verse.text: The heart is deceitful above all things and beyond cure. Who can understand it? I the LORD search the heart and examine the mind, to reward each person according to their conduct, according to what their deeds deserve.

reflection.scripture: The heart is deceitful above all things and beyond cure. Who can understand it? I the LORD search the heart and examine the mind, to reward each person according to their conduct, according to what their deeds deserve.
reflection.observation: Jeremiah doesn't sugarcoat the human condition — our hearts are naturally bent toward self-deception. We rationalize, justify, and hide our true motives even from ourselves. But the passage pivots to hope: God searches and examines. He sees what we cannot. His discernment penetrates what our own self-awareness misses.
reflection.application: Invite God into the places you normally keep hidden — the justifications, hidden resentments, small compromises. Instead of self-diagnosing your heart, ask God to search it. Before making a decision today, pause and ask: 'What would my motive look like if I couldn't hide it from God?'
reflection.prayer: Lord, You know my heart better than I know it myself. Search me — the parts I proudly display and the corners I try to keep hidden. I don't want to live deceived by my own justifications. Give me the courage to face what You reveal, and the grace to let You reshape what You find. In Jesus' name, Amen.
